findings.where: First screen (hero) at both widths, the nav (Profile, Articles, Blog only), and the foot of the article specimen; the parts map shows no mailto link or contact control anywhere on the page
findings.fault: There is no way to reach Mark anywhere on the page. The first screen has no action at all and does not show the address Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com. The nav has no Contact item, and the article ends without a contact route. The palette and texture notes describe a pad-yellow 'address strip' at the foot of the sheet, but no such strip was built. The brief's tile format requires the first screen to show one action with the address.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank staff member who has decided Mark might fit their terms of reference has no visible way to write to him and must leave to look for an address. The founder would object too: the personal-advisor test asks for 'one direct, personal way to reach him', and the brief requires the address to be shown.

findings.where: First screen, the heading 'In my view, we are at a turning point in the story of public-private partnerships.' and what follows it
findings.fault: The heading promises a view: what the turning point is and what Mark thinks about it. Nothing on the first screen delivers it or points to it. No link leads to the piece that makes the argument, and the line below changes the subject to a list of who he advises. A reader is left with an opinion they cannot follow up.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who wants to judge Mark's thinking quickly. The heading makes them curious, but they then have to guess which nav item (Articles or Blog) holds the argument, so the heading reads as a slogan rather than an entry into his work.

findings.where: First screen, the credential line under the name ('Formerly Lead Lawyer, PPP Group, World Bank') and the supporting paragraph
findings.fault: The only proof on the first screen is one past job title. It does not say where Mark works or is based (no country, no regions), and it shows no recent work or talk with its venue. There is no third-party proof and no link out to work that named bodies host. A first-time visitor cannot tell that he has done this kind of work for bodies like theirs, in their region.
findings.who_objects: A visitor from a development bank who selects against terms of reference by region and project type. They have to dig through the Profile before they can tell whether Mark is relevant, and an unproven claim of advising 'banks and governments' reads as an adjective rather than as evidence.

findings.where: Article specimen, the Download row ('Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge — Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF')
findings.fault: The newest talk is listed with a date but no venue or host, so it does nothing to show who asked Mark to speak.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader, for whom 'who asked' is the strongest standing signal. Without a venue, a lecture is just a file.
